rationale:
M14 ONTOLOGY, `exports`, second spelling. `cpp/exports-visibility-attribute` pins the two VENDOR KEYWORD forms (`__declspec(dllexport)`, `__attribute__((visibility("default")))`); this pins the form the C++11 STANDARD defines — `[[gnu::visibility("default")]]` and `[[msvc::dllexport]]` — which matters because of an upstream fact neither fixture could see on its own:

  `src/ast/engine.ts` blanks `__attribute__((...))` and `__declspec(...)` out of C/C++ content BEFORE the parser sees it (the 'UNIVERSAL C/C++ AST ILLUSION FIX' block, ~lines 1388-1393). Measured over 929 corpus files: production `parseFile` delivers 0 `exports` rows, while the same analyzer over the un-blanked text delivers 1 — the corpus's only export-marked declaration. The `[[...]]` spelling is NOT blanked, so it is the only arm that can reach production today, and this fixture is what proves it: 4 rows through `parseFile` on this file.

  THE READ IS A NODE WALK, and the measured shape is why. On the pinned fork the `[[...]]` form is `attribute_declaration > attribute > (identifier vendor, identifier NAME, argument_list > string_literal)`, so the attribute's NAME is its LAST identifier (`gnu::visibility` -> `visibility`) and the argument is read from the `argument_list` node. A text scan would have to guess where the vendor ends, and this lane holds zero regexes (D6) precisely because text rules match comments and string literals.

  THE ARMS THAT COST EDGES ARE THE NEGATIVES, and they are chosen from the corpus's own histogram rather than invented. Over the 912 cpp files of cpp-example + cpp-sample + fmt + googletest + nlohmann-json there are 308 `attribute_declaration` nodes: `nodiscard` 285, `maybe_unused` 9, `noreturn` 8, `deprecated` 6, and ZERO `visibility` or `dllexport`. A rule reading 'this declaration carries an attribute' would therefore manufacture ~4 edges per class on real code while the true population is 0 — so the four non-export attribute names are pinned as forbids, at file scope and at class scope. `visibility("hidden")` and `visibility("protected")` separate on the ARGUMENT STRING, which is the node that distinguishes them, and `extern "C"` is pinned because it is language LINKAGE, not visibility.

expectRelationships.note: `[[gnu::visibility("default")]]` at file scope. This row survives the production entry: engine.ts blanks the `__attribute__((...))` form and not this one.
`[[msvc::dllexport]]` — the last identifier of the `attribute` is the attribute NAME, and the vendor prefix `msvc::` is not part of it.
on a CLASS, written between the keyword and the name (`struct [[...]] Name`). The attribute_declaration is a named child of the specifier, which is why the class arm consults the same helper.

on a MEMBER: the endpoint is `Owner.member` so an exported member is not confused with a same-named file-scope entity. The persister binds this by leaf (`member`), which the ontology census measures as 100% resolved.

expectRelationshipCount.note: EXACT count, because `expectRelationships` means '>= 1 match' and only an exact count can fail on a duplicate. One attribute, one declaration, one edge — the same D3 rule `cpp/one-edge-per-pair-959` pins for `contains`.

forbidRelationships.note: THE DIRECTION THAT COSTS EDGES. `[[nodiscard]]` is 285 of the corpus's 308 `[[...]]` attributes; a rule reading 'carries an attribute' instead of the attribute's NAME would manufacture an export edge for essentially every annotated declaration in C++.

`visibility("hidden")` is the OPPOSITE of exported. Same attribute, same node shape, opposite meaning — so the arm that separates them is the argument STRING read from the argument_list node, and this forbid row is what makes that arm a gate rather than a description.
`visibility("protected")` is a real visibility this analyzer does not claim to read. Emitting it would be inventing an export.

`extern "C"` is language LINKAGE: it changes the symbol name the linker sees and says nothing about visibility. An analyzer that conflated the two would claim every C-ABI function exports from a shared library.

`__declspec(dllimport)` is the opposite DIRECTION: this translation unit imports the symbol. The engine blanks the spelling before the parser, so this row also documents that the forbid is a language rule rather than a blanking artefact.
